text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty P-9421 fired for service=az2-serving (az2-serving-degrade) — automated threshold: 5xx-rate > 2% over 60s. Paging oncall @alice. link: https://pd.company/p/9421 :rotating_light:

alice (oncall): acked. I'm on it. checking dashboards and recent deploys.

incident-bot: Ack recorded by alice at 1769365440. Escalation timer paused.

bob (sre): I can see a sharp uptick in 5xx from the az2 inference pool. KV cache eviction rates spike, then nodes dropping. Metrics: cpu steady, gpunet errors up.

alice (oncall): logs show repeated gRPC 14 / 'connection reset' on host az2-gpu-12. sample tail:
```
2026-03-15T18:10:22Z az2-gpu-12 inference-server ERROR rpc: conn reset by peer
2026-03-15T18:10:23Z az2-gpu-12 runtime INFO kvcache: eviction triggered, freed 12 shards
2026-03-15T18:10:24Z az2-gpu-12 autoscaler WARN scale-down denied: active requests > 0
```
Looks like thrash + network blips.

carol (platform): hypothesis: NIC firmware bug + autoscaler reacting, causing short-term capacity loss. We should consider activating routing fallback to az1 for production traffic and enable conservative autoscaler mode for az2.

alice (oncall): what's the customer impact? eve, any support signals?

eve (support): I'm seeing 3 enterprise customers with repeated errors on /v1/generate in last 10m (incidents opened). Error rate for hosted-api from eu-west/az2 region jumped from 0.3% -> 2.8%. Not yet widespread, but one high-traffic customer (acct: acme-corp) reports degraded latency and some truncated responses.

frank (eng-lead): If we divert, is there capacity in az1? We should avoid cold-popping more nodes. Carol, can you run a capacity check?

carol (platform): quick check output:
```
> ./infra/tools/cap-check --region az1 --model default --min-ready
az1: ready GPUs=24, headroom=18%
az2: ready GPUs=8, headroom=6% (degrading)
```
az1 has headroom but not a ton. Options:
- partial divert (10-20%) to az1 + enable prefix/KV cache bypass for diverted requests
- full failover (risky, cold starts)

bob (sre): recommended plan: 1) enable routing fallback policy at the edge to prefer az2 but divert on repeated 5xx (3 attempts) — fast mitigation. 2) set az2 autoscaler to 'conservative' to stop thrash. 3) open PD high severity if we lose more nodes.

alice (oncall): I'll activate the routing fallback now and flip autoscaler. stepping through commands:

- enable fallback rule (edge-admin):
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://edge.company/api/v1/routes/fallback \
  -d '{"service":"hosted-api","from_region":"az2","to_region":"az1","on_5xx":3}'
```
- set autoscaler mode for az2:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch configmap/autoscaler --type merge -p '{"data":{"mode":"conservative-evict-delay"}}'
```

alice (oncall): done. edge rule submitted, autoscaler patch applied. Monitoring for immediate change.

incident-bot: Routing fallback rule change queued (change-id: cf-7765). Autoscaler config rolled (cfg-9933).

alice (oncall): within 90s we see 5xx rate drop from 2.8% -> 1.1%. error spikes shifting to az1 somewhat. No new node terminations in az2 for last 2m.

eve (support): acme-corp reports partial improvement, latency still a bit high but errors reduced. Support is updating customers.

bob (sre): good. keep fallback enabled for 30m, then reassess. I'll open a granular alert to watch kvcache eviction and NIC errors (gpunet).

frank (eng-lead): also want a quick postmortem note drafted once we stabilize. Possible action items: schedule NIC firmware batch, autoscaler tuning, and consider warm spare capacity in neighboring regions.

carol (platform): filing an internal mitigation runbook entry and noting exact cfg IDs: cf-7765 (fallback rule), cfg-9933 (autoscaler). Also capturing PD timeline.

alice (oncall): handing off to dave for continued watch — I've been on call ~40m and need to rotate. dave, please take the thread and keep an eye for re-escalation.

dave (oncall-second): taking handoff. I've seen the rule in edge UI, and az1 keys warmed ~60s after divert. I'll keep the fallback on and monitor until load normalizes. If az2 nodes continue to drop, I'll escalate to on-call lead.

incident-bot: Handoff recorded: from alice to dave at 1769365902.

bob (sre): quick run of node health in az2 shows 2 hosts with repeated NIC errors: az2-gpu-12 and az2-gpu-17. Marking them unschedulable to avoid further thrash:
```bash
kubectl cordon az2-gpu-12
kubectl cordon az2-gpu-17
```
Note: cordon only; will not drain unless we want to move workloads.

dave (oncall-second): cordoned. Observability shows 5xx trending down to 0.6% across region. Keeping fallback active.

frank (eng-lead): good work. please do not fully failover unless SLO breach. Communicate to affected customers that we're mitigating and will follow up with root cause.

carol (platform): creating PD incident doc and labeling for postmortem (az2-nic-thrash-20260315). I'll attach metrics and runbooks.

incident-bot: PagerDuty P-9421 status: acknowledged -> mitigated (fallback active). Will remain open for post-incident review.

dave (oncall-second): I'll maintain this watch for the next 60m and then drop the fallback if metrics stable for 30m. If anything changes I'll re-notify in this thread.

alice (oncall): thanks team. leaving the channel. :thumbsup:

frank (eng-lead): thanks all. action items: (1) patch NIC firmware schedule (carol), (2) autoscaler tuning PR (bob), (3) add warm spare guidance to capacity playbook (frank).

incident-bot: Next steps reminder set: 24h postmortem checklist due and owner assigned.
